title: herdr tests burn the full confirm wait for a dispatch that never spawns an agent
description:
internal/exec/herdr/harness_test.go:590 sets ConfirmTimeout to 1 second. After the prompt, Start waits for the agent to reach 'working' (internal/exec/herdr/gate.go:131). The fake herdr server polls a status file every 25ms and reports 'idle' while the file is absent; harnessOptions.spawnAgent defaults FALSE, so in most tests nothing ever writes it and the wait burns the full second. The harness comment at :586 says so outright - 'the confirm wait, which a dispatch with no visible work burns in full'.

Estimated 70-85s of internal/exec/herdr's 185s: roughly 40% of the package spent waiting for workers that were never started.

The fix is not a shorter timeout - the wait is real behaviour worth testing. It is that a test dispatching no agent should not wait for one: let the harness say it spawns nothing and skip the confirm, or have the fake server answer definitively instead of staying silent.
